newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Feb money growth shows slow economy - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Japan Feb money growth shows slow economy - analysts.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth of 3.0 percent in February, at the lower end of economists' forecasts, reflected sluggishness in the underlying trends of the domestic economy, analysts said on Tuesday.
The Bank of Japan said broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CD) grew a preliminary 3.0 percent year-on-year in February.
This was below the revised figure of 3.2 percent growth in January and at the lower end of the 3.0 to 3.3 percent range of forecasts for February by economists polled by Reuters.

"The money supply figures may indicate that the economy could stay weak from the start of the new fiscal year (in April)," said Yoshito Sakakibara, economist at Salomon Brothers Asia Ltd. "There is a possiblity that the (M2+CD) growth may fall below 3.0 percent in the coming months."

A Bank of Japan official told reporters that the money supply figures were in line with the central bank's prediction that money supply growth would remain in the three to four percent range during the January-March period.
The BOJ official said the figures reflected the bank's view that the domestic economy was in a gradual improvement trend.
But the analysts were more pessimistic about the outlook for the domestic economy.
"I thought the figure would be higher than 3.0 percent (in February)," said Atsushi Takeda, a researcher at DKB Research Institute Corp.

"The declining trend in bank deposits seems to be putting downward pressure on overall money growth," he added. "The trend of individuals and corporations shifting their funds out of bank deposits and into foreign bonds may be continuing."
Takeda said M2+CD growth is expected to remain around 3.0 percent for the immediate future.
"There is a possiblity that growth may fall a bit below 3.0 percent in April and May, but I don't expect this will be a major trend," he said.
"I believe that the basic trend of the economy is not weak and that money supply growth should be picking up towards the end of the year," he added.
